## Stage counts
These print to stderr only if you run with `REPORT_DEBUG=1`; otherwise the script is silent.

| Stage | Count |
|---|---|
| Order rows (blank lines excluded) | 1842 |
| Malformed | 41 |
| Valid | 1801 (1842 − 41) |
| Distinct ids | 1445 → 356 duplicates removed |
| Cancelled | 191 |
| Test | 362 |
| Included | 892 (191 + 362 + 892 = 1445) |
| Refund rows | 159: 5 repeated ids, 123 matched, 31 ignored, 0 bad |
| Total gross / total refunds | $117,375.98 / $9,616.98 → rate 0.0819 |

**Malformed rows (41), one cause each:**
- 8 with the wrong number of fields (4 had 13, 4 had 11)
- 5 with an empty `order_id`
- 8 bad quantities (`-1` ×4, `two` ×3, `n/a`)
- 4 bad unit prices (`abc` ×2, `12,99x`, empty)
- 4 bad currencies (`JPY` ×3, `EURO`)
- 8 bad `order_date` values (`2025-13-04` ×2, `30/02` ×2, `31/02` ×2, `n/a`, `yesterday`)
- 4 bad `updated_at` values (`2025-02-30…` ×2, `soon`, empty)

Comparing `updated_at` as real instants matters. A plain string comparison would have picked a different winning version for 60 orders.

## Gap decisions and how many rows each affected
- **Strict whitespace:** only currency, status, `is_test` and the `test-` prefix are stripped and case-folded. This rejected 0 rows; no other field had stray spaces.
- **Email domain:** the text after the last `@`, compared case-insensitively to exactly `test.shopco.io`. The only near miss is `latest.shopco.io`, which is kept as a real customer.
- **Ties on the same `updated_at` instant:** the row read last wins. There were 0 ties.
- **Bad refund rows:** none.
- **Repeated refund ids:** 5 later copies dropped, keeping the first.
- **No cap on refunds:** a refund larger than the order's gross is applied in full, so net revenue can go negative. I didn't count how many orders this affected.
- **Quarter keys:** only the four 2025 keys appear, because every valid order is dated 2025.
- **Product ties:** broken alphabetically; there was no tie for top product.

## Data the README didn't cover
- `Testa, Maria` is the only name that starts with "test" but not "test-", so she counts as a real customer, as the README says.
- Four orders have `updated_at` in 2026. They are used normally for dedupe and keep their 2025 quarter from `order_date`.
- Six refunds are dated 2026 and still count against their orders.
- Six refunds point at unknown `ORD-9…` ids. They are part of the 31 ignored refunds, along with refunds to cancelled or test orders.
- The refunds file had no bad amounts or currencies. The script would skip them if a future export has any.
